title: Introduce harmonic token system for interactive states and density-aware components
creator: Ana Park
description:
Overview:
Redwood's component library has accumulated multiple bespoke token ramps for color, type, spacing, and elevation. This ticket proposes a single 'harmonic' token system that re-centers interactive state colors, a compact density scale, and micro-elevation steps to reduce visual noise while improving accessibility and migration predictability. The goal is a coherent, composable token surface that: (1) gives clear interactive affordances (hover/pressed/focus/disabled), (2) compresses spacing/radius variants into a density axis, and (3) introduces uniform micro-elevation that maps to functional layers (controls, overlays, data rows).

Scope:
- Define a new color ramp for interactive states (primary/neutral/cta) with anchored contrast targets for focus and disabled states.
- Publish a density token axis (dense / default / spacious) that adjusts spacing, radius, and small-type scale offsets.
- Introduce 3 micro-elevation steps (+ subtle ambient shadow) mapped to: surface, control, and floating-data layers.
- Update core components: Button, Table row, Card, Tooltip, Chart legend item to consume tokens.
- Provide migration plan and codemods for existing components and internal pages.

Why now:
- Recent customer feedback: dense dashboards in Dedicated customers look visually inconsistent across components.
- Observability shows 18% of routes render with mixed legacy tokens leading to contrast regressions on dark-bg charts.
- We need a single migration path to support both hosted and private deployments with minimal runtime toggles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Token spec published in the design tokens repo with JSON and CSS variables and mapped semantic names (e.g., color.interactive.primary.hover).
- Figma library populated with token styles and a small pattern library demonstrating density toggles.
- Buttons, Table rows, and Cards updated in the component repo with unit and visual tests (percy snapshots) and documented variant behavior.
- Accessibility checks: all interactive state contrasts >= 3:1 for non-text UI, 4.5:1 for text where applicable; keyboard focus visible and consistent.
- Migration guide + codemod PRs that convert 80% of internal usages in core app repos (2-week canary).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We are intentionally choosing 3 elevation micro-steps to limit cognitive overhead; this reduces flexibility but increases predictability for implementers.
- Compression of spacing variants may require minor layout adjustments in older pages; we will provide a 'legacy-density' flag for enterprise customers during rollout.
- Quantized color ramps optimize for common chart palettes; extreme custom palettes may require mapping utilities.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge token spec and Figma styles (design).
2) Implement tokens in component library behind a feature flag; run visual regression baseline.
3) Execute codemod on internal shells + 2 pilot customer dashboards.
4) Remove legacy tokens and turn feature flag on by default after two-week monitoring window.

Migration helpers:
- Codemod: repo link placeholder https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokens-codemod (PR draft).
- Migration dashboard: https://internal.redwood.dev/migrations/DES-31207 (tracking page).
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/harmonic-tokens — contains density switch prototypes.

Open questions:
- Should elevation tokens include color-tinting on dark surfaces for improved depth perception? (UX asked to prototype two variants).
- Do we expose density as a global CSS class or as per-component prop in the React library? (Engineering prefers class for perf).

Next steps:
- Finalize contrast targets with accessibility engineer.
- Engineer sign-off on runtime token switch performance cost.
- Schedule two pilot migrations with Platform team (ENG-4120).
comments: 2025-02-05 — Ana Park: Initial draft posted to Figma and tokens repo. Shared with PM and Infra. Link added to description.

2025-02-12 — Marcus Liu: Engineering review notes: prefer density as CSS class to avoid prop drilling; raised a worry about bundle size if tokens are shipped as separate CSS variables per component. Requested perf numbers for runtime switching.

2025-02-18 — Priya Nair (Accessibility): Ran contrast sweeps on the proposed interactive ramps. Hover states meet 3:1 non-text threshold, suggestion: increase primary.focus contrast to 4.5:1 for small icon labels. See confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ACC/Harmonic+Tokens+Contrast

2025-02-25 — Marcus Liu: Prototype implementation in components repo (branch: harmonic-tokens/feature). Created PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/components/pull/472. Percy snapshots attached. Some table row variants required 2px to 3px spacing adjustments in dense mode.

2025-03-01 — Design review session: PMs (Lena Ortiz), Platform Eng (Jamal Reed), and Security attended. Consensus: proceed with class-based density + legacy flag for enterprise. Security asked for token naming audit; added to dependencies.

2025-03-05 — Marcus Liu: Addressed feedback, pushed updated codemod and added automatic fallback mapping for legacy token names. Marking this ticket 'In Review' pending final accessibility sign-off and one pilot migration run.
Follow-ups (post-merge): Create a short video walkthrough for internal engineers on density decisions and codemod usage; schedule a 1-hour drop-in migration assistance window.
